name: BioHyalux

card.summary: A hyaluronic acid dermal filler gel injected by clinicians to smooth folds such as the nasolabial lines and restore facial volume.
card.note: Injectable fillers are procedures with risks such as bruising and, rarely, vascular occlusion; performed by licensed clinicians.

quick.overview:
BioHyalux is a hyaluronic acid (HA) gel filler. HA is a water-binding sugar that, in cross-linked form, is injected under the skin to fill lines and add volume. The visible payoff is smoother folds such as the nasolabial folds.

A multicentre randomised trial in Chinese adults compared BioHyalux with Restylane on opposite sides of the face for nasolabial folds, designed to test whether the new gel was non-inferior.[1] General reviews of HA fillers describe their use across facial layers.[2]
quick.how: HA fillers are injected by trained clinicians with needles or cannulas into targeted facial areas; results appear right away and fade over months as the body breaks the gel down.[3] Practitioners choose gel firmness by area.
quick.risks: Documented effects of HA fillers include bruising, redness, itching and swelling; rarer complications include vascular occlusion, nerve or vessel injury and granulomatous reactions.[3] They are medical procedures and are regulated as devices or drugs depending on the country.

lead: BioHyalux is a hyaluronic acid-based dermal filler. Hyaluronic acid absorbs water and swells into a gel, which makes it useful for filling facial wrinkles and restoring volume.[3]

Its main published clinical study is a 2016 multicentre, double-blind, randomised, controlled non-inferiority trial in 88 subjects with moderate to severe nasolabial folds, comparing BioHyalux with Restylane, with each product injected on one side of the face.[1]

Wikipedia notes that HA filler effects last roughly 6 to 12 months and that the US FDA has approved the use class.[3] Reviews describe how HA fillers are used to treat aging changes across facial anatomical layers.[2]

chain: Gel injected into folds or volume-depleted areas
Fills and lifts the treated tissue
angle.text: The filler is used to soften nasolabial lines and restore volume. Clinicians choose the area and product for the desired contour.

paras: HA is a naturally occurring polysaccharide. Native HA breaks down quickly in the body, so fillers use cross-linking and chemical stabilisation to extend duration.[3] Rheology (flow and firmness) differs between products and affects where they are used.[4]
Cosmetic filler use targets nasolabial folds and other facial regions as the face ages.[1][2]
HA fillers can cause pain, bruising, redness and itching; vascular occlusion and granulomatous foreign-body reactions are rarer complications.[3]
A randomised, double-blind, multicentre non-inferiority trial in 88 Chinese subjects compared BioHyalux with Restylane in nasolabial folds, assessing efficacy, safety and durability.[1]

timeline.event: Randomised trial comparing BioHyalux with Restylane published.[1]
